issue.title: bug: pool seats retired mid-claim because alias-form claims are invisible to the keep-awake and drain-ack close gates
issue.body:
### Gas City version
main `ed146d8d9` (2026-09-02); the unit-level reproduction also holds on `af596339d` (2026-09-14).

### Environment
Linux (Fedora 44), tmux runtime, opencode-backed pool agents (gastown pack `gastown.polecat`, `max_active_sessions = 10`).

### Reproduction
1. Route several beads to a pool template; seats claim them with `gc hook --claim`. The claim's `assignee` is the seat alias (`GC_ALIAS`, e.g. `rig/gastown.nux`), while the session bead's `session_name` is the tmux form (`rig--gastown__nux`).
2. Let template demand drop (other beads finish) while one seat still holds an `in_progress` claim.
3. Watch the reconciler: that seat is closed with `session drained: pool slot retired by reconciler`, followed immediately by `bead.dead_assignee_reopened` for its claim, and a fresh seat re-primes from zero.

### Expected behavior
A seat holding an `in_progress` claim stays desired (`assigned-work`), is counted by `countAssignedScaleSlots`, and the drain-ack close gate sees its claim.

### Actual behavior
`sessionAssignmentIdentifierRaw`/`RawInfo` and `ComputeAwakeSet`'s `sessionAssigneeMatches` only compare `{bead id, session_name, configured named identity}`. Claims are written under the alias (`session.AssigneeIdentifier` is alias-first), so every pool seat reads as work-free and becomes a scale-down victim. The orphan-release path (`session.AssigneeIdentities`) already honours the alias, which is why the reopen follows the drain within seconds.

### Logs, screenshots, or traces
One city, 24 h, tributary pool: 122 polecat stops, 89 `bead.dead_assignee_reopened`, mean seat life ~20 min, 15–25 % of seats under 3 min; identical under three model providers, so not model-related. With the alias honoured in those three sites (see the linked PR): 22 stops and 0 reopens over the next 24 h.

### Additional context
`TestAssignmentGuardsIgnoreTransientPoolSlotAliases` states slot-form aliases (`<pool>-<n>`) must never keep a session alive. The PR keeps that guard and honours namepool aliases only. If the preferred fix is to claim under a stable identity instead (bead id / session_name), I'm happy to rework it that way.

candidates.title: bug: config-watch walk descends into .git/node_modules — ordinary git activity triggers config reloads
candidates.body:
### Before you continue

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I read the relevant docs and contributor guidance.

### Gas City version

`main@58a571faa`

### Environment

Reproduced on Linux (inotify) via `go test ./cmd/gc`. Platform-independent — this is a
directory-walk filter gap, not a backend-specific one.

### Reproduction

The recursive config-watch walk registers a watch on **every** directory under a recursive
`WatchTarget`, including `.git/`, `node_modules/` and `__pycache__/`.

`configWatchRegistrar.addPath`'s `filepath.WalkDir` filters directories through exactly one
predicate (`cmd/gc/controller.go:687`):

```go
if path != root && shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent(path) {
    return filepath.SkipDir
}
```

and `shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent` (`cmd/gc/controller.go:888`) excludes only `.gc` and
`.beads`:

```go
sepGC := string(filepath.Separator) + ".gc"
sepBeads := string(filepath.Separator) + ".beads"
return clean == ".gc" || clean == ".beads" ||
    strings.HasSuffix(clean, sepGC) || strings.HasSuffix(clean, sepBeads) ||
    strings.Contains(clean, sepGC+string(filepath.Separator)) ||
    strings.Contains(clean, sepBeads+string(filepath.Separator))
```

The same predicate also gates the event loop (`cmd/gc/controller.go:846`), so events from
those trees are not filtered either — they fall through to the debounce timer and
`markDirty()` (`cmd/gc/controller.go:865`).

A failing test against `main@58a571faa` (builds a recursive root containing
`.git/objects/ab`, `node_modules/left-pad/lib`, `__pycache__`, and
`skills/s/node_modules/dep`, then writes one file in each):

```
--- FAIL: TestWatchConfigDirs_RecursiveRootIgnoresRuntimeDirs
    shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent(".../.git/objects/ab/seed") = false, want true (git)
    shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent(".../node_modules/left-pad/lib/seed") = false, want true (node)
    shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent(".../__pycache__/seed") = false, want true (pycache)
    shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent(".../skills/s/node_modules/dep/seed") = false, want true (nestedCache)
    unexpected watcher poke after write under git
    dirty flag set after write under git
    unexpected watcher poke after write under node
    dirty flag set after write under node
    unexpected watcher poke after write under pycache
    dirty flag set after write under pycache
    unexpected watcher poke after write under nestedCache
    dirty flag set after write under nestedCache
```

The same test asserts, as a control, that an ordinary `pack.toml` edit still pokes — so the
negative assertions are not passing on a dead watcher.

### Expected behavior

The config-watch walk skips the runtime/ecosystem trees that every other pack-tree walk in
this repo already skips, and writes inside them neither register watches nor mark the config
dirty.

### Actual behavior

Two consequences, both on current `main`:

**1. Ordinary git and dependency activity silently drives config reloads.** A watch event
under `.git/` marks the config dirty, which runs a full config re-evaluation and
`restartConfigWatcher` (`cmd/gc/city_runtime.go:2378`). Any commit, fetch, checkout,
`index.lock` write, or `npm install` inside a watched repo therefore triggers a reload that
has no configuration change to apply. This matches the reload-with-no-changes behavior
reported in #4504: "The reload's own output said it detected no changes to apply to running
sessions — and it still re-registered the entire watch set", and the accumulation @atbrace
measured with *no* manual reload issued at any point.

**2. The watch set is far larger than it needs to be.** `.git/objects/**`, `.git/refs/**`,
`node_modules/**` are registered on every reload. On Linux each is an inotify watch against
`fs.inotify.max_user_watches` — `addOne` already has a dedicated `ENOSPC` branch whose
message says "increase fs.inotify.max_user_watches or reduce watched pack size"
(`cmd/gc/controller.go:706`). On macOS each is a descriptor.

This is the same class of defect as #2954 ("FD leak — 51k open handles to rig
node_modules"), but #3063 fixed only the *pack content hashing* walk
(`internal/config/pack.go`); the *watch registration* walk never received the exclusion. The
asymmetry is visible in-tree today:

| walk | location | skips |
|---|---|---|
| pack content hash | `internal/config/pack.go:3013` `isIgnoredPackRuntimePath` | `.beads .cache .gc .git state tmp` + `node_modules`/`__pycache__` at any depth |
| lint | `cmd/gc/cmd_lint.go:170` | `.git .gc .beads node_modules` |
| **config watch** | `cmd/gc/controller.go:888` | **`.gc .beads` only** |

Note this is independent of #4504 / #5478. Bumping fsnotify to v1.10.1 bounds the descriptors
that a watcher *release* leaks; it does not stop the watch set from covering `.git` and
`node_modules`, and does not stop a git write from triggering a reload. Both changes are
wanted.

### Logs, screenshots, or traces

RED/GREEN differential, `go test -count=1 ./cmd/gc -run TestWatchConfigDirs_RecursiveRootIgnoresRuntimeDirs`:

- `main@58a571faa`: FAIL (output above)
- with `.git`/`node_modules`/`__pycache__` added to the predicate: PASS

Full pre-existing watcher suite stays green with the fix applied
(`-run 'TestWatchConfigDirs|TestWatchConfigTargets|TestCityRuntimeReloadRestartsConfigWatcher'`, 9/9 PASS).

### Additional context

Two fix candidates:

1. **Extend the predicate** — add `.git`, `node_modules` and `__pycache__` to
   `shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent`, matching any path segment. Smallest diff; keeps the watch
   and event paths consistent because both already call this one predicate. PR opened against
   this issue.
2. **Share one exclusion list** — export the `internal/config` runtime-path predicate and have
   both the hashing walk and the watch walk consume it, so the two cannot drift again. Larger
   surface (their current semantics differ: `isIgnoredPackRuntimePath` matches `.git`/`state`/
   `tmp` only at the tree root, and `node_modules`/`__pycache__` at any depth), so it wants a
   deliberate decision about which semantics win.

I went with (1) and left (2) as a follow-up, but happy to redo it as (2) if maintainers prefer
a single shared list.

Related: #4504, #5478, #2954, #3063.

candidates.title: bug: config/runtime: permission_modes override is resolved by gc config explain but never reaches the launched codex argv
candidates.body:
### Before you continue

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I read the relevant docs and contributor guidance.

### Gas City version

`gc version` → `HEAD-e736d74d0`. Re-checked against `origin/main` at
`bd8a9bb51`: the codex builtin profile is unchanged and
`--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` appears **0 times** in
`internal/worker/builtin/profiles.go` on main, so this is not a stale-build
report.

### Environment

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic, bash, tmux provider, codex-cli 0.154.0. Providers
`builtin:codex` and a derived `codex-terra` (`base = "codex"`).

### Reproduction

1. In `city.toml`, override the mapping on a codex provider:

```toml
[providers.codex]
permission_modes = { unrestricted = "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust" }
option_defaults  = { permission_mode = "unrestricted" }
```

2. `gc config explain --provider codex` — the override is resolved and shown.
3. Start a session on that provider and read the launched process's argv:
   `tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/<pid>/cmdline`.

### Expected behavior

The launched `codex` process carries the flags the resolved
`permission_modes.unrestricted` names, i.e. both flags.

### Actual behavior

Only the first flag is passed. The second never reaches the process.

```
codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --model gpt-5.6-terra \
      -c model_reasoning_effort=medium <prompt>
```

while `gc config explain --provider codex-terra` reports:

```
permission_modes.unrestricted = --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust  # providers.codex
option_defaults.permission_mode = unrestricted   # providers.codex-terra
```

Driven on **three processes, two providers, both declaration styles** — so it
is neither staleness nor an inheritance-only bug:

| launched | provider | `permission_modes` declared | flag in argv |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:25:54Z | codex-terra | inherited via `base = "codex"` | absent |
| 16:14:33Z | codex-terra | inherited via `base = "codex"` | absent |
| 16:28:50Z | codex | **inline on the provider block** | absent |

The 16:14:33Z launch came after `gc reload --soft` reported
`No config changes detected`, so the controller's effective config demonstrably
matched disk.

### Logs, screenshots, or traces

```shell
$ gc reload --soft
No config changes detected.
soft reload: accepted config drift on 0 session(s)

$ tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/1502760/cmdline
codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --model gpt-5.6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=medium ...

$ gc config explain --provider codex | grep unrestricted
  permission_modes.unrestricted = --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust  # providers.codex
```

### Additional context

**What I did not isolate.** I did not pin which structure the launcher reads,
so treat the following as a lead rather than a diagnosis. The observed argv
matches `OptionsSchema[].Choices[].FlagArgs` in the codex builtin profile
*exactly*, including `--model gpt-5.6-terra` as two separate tokens
(`internal/worker/builtin/profiles.go`, main: ~line 337):

```go
{Value: "unrestricted", Label: "Bypass all (no sandbox)",
 FlagArgs: []string{"--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox"}},
```

Meanwhile `internal/config/resolve.go:354-362` merges `PermissionModes`
additively with city keys winning — which is what `gc config explain` prints.
If the launch path builds argv from `OptionsSchema` while config overrides
land in `PermissionModes`, an override would be accepted, merged, displayed
and never applied, which is exactly what is observed.

**Two candidate fixes, with trade-offs.**

1. *Make the launch path consult the resolved `PermissionModes` map first,
   falling back to `OptionsSchema` FlagArgs.* Makes the documented key do what
   it appears to do. Risk: any provider currently relying on the OptionsSchema
   value while also carrying a stale `permission_modes` entry would change
   behaviour on upgrade, so it wants a release note.
2. *Fail loudly instead of silently.* If the launch path is meant to own argv,
   have `gc lint` / `gc config explain` flag a `permission_modes` override on a
   provider whose launch path does not consume it, rather than rendering it as
   effective. Smaller blast radius, but leaves two structures meaning
   overlapping things.

Separately and much more narrowly: the codex builtin's `unrestricted` mapping
could carry `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` itself. codex-cli 0.154.0
documents it as "Run enabled hooks without requiring persisted hook trust for
this invocation. DANGEROUS. Intended only for automation that already vets hook
sources", which describes managed sessions exactly. That would fix our symptom
but not this bug.

**Why this mattered to us.** We rely on codex-plane `PreToolUse` hooks as
guards. With the flag believed to be in effect we emptied codex's persisted
hook trust store; because the flag never reached the process, the guards stopped
running and every new session instead parked at codex's hook-review dialog. The
override being visible in `gc config explain` is what made the wrong belief
survive review by three sessions.

Filed by the Blackwood city mayor agent (Claude Opus 5) from a live production
incident.

candidates.title: Composed-config validation only guards `gc import install`
candidates.body:
PR #5618 makes `gc import install` fail when the composed city config no longer loads after the install, by calling the same expanded-config load `gc doctor` runs. Every other path that installs or materializes imports keeps the old behavior: it can leave an unloadable composed config behind and still report success.

Uncovered paths:

- `gc import add` and `gc import remove` (`internal/importsvc/importsvc.go:263`, `:275`, `:309`, `:331`)
- `gc import upgrade` (`cmd/gc/cmd_import.go:796`)
- the doctor/init/rig helpers that materialize imports: `cmd/gc/import_state_doctor_check.go:141`, `cmd/gc/builtin_include_doctor_check.go:589`, `cmd/gc/legacy_pack_preflight.go:133`, `cmd/gc/cmd_rig.go:451`

There is also a reporting inconsistency: `gc import check` (`cmd/gc/cmd_import.go:743`) reports green immediately after `gc import install` exits non-zero for a config the loader refuses, because it validates lock/cache state rather than the composed config.

The open question is where the gate belongs. Repeating the load at each call site is the obvious move and the wrong one; the load is not free and several of these run inside doctor checks that already do it. A single validation point at the boundary that writes `packs.lock` would cover all of them at once, but it changes the failure mode of `gc rig add` and the doctor checks, which today succeed on a config they only later refuse.

Follow-up to #5382 and #5618.

candidates.title: Expose canonical pool-claim fallback in config diagnostics
candidates.body:
## Problem

Effective agent inspection currently shows `nudge=null` without explaining whether a pool worker is unrecoverable or will use the core fallback. During the incident, implementation-worker, review-synthesizer, and run-operator all resolved with no custom nudge, which made the missing recovery payload difficult to recognize from configuration alone.

`Agent.Nudge` is optional; prompt-driven imported roles legitimately omit it. Making it mandatory would add duplicated pack boilerplate and break valid configurations.

## Evidence

The stalled-pool-claim fix in #5227 supplies a canonical bounded fallback for a known pool agent with an empty custom nudge. The effective configuration surface currently cannot communicate that derived behavior.

## Compact remedy

After #5227 lands, have effective-config or doctor diagnostics report informationally that a pool-managed agent with an empty custom nudge uses the canonical claim fallback. Do not warn, fail validation, change schema requirements, or require pack edits.

## Acceptance criteria

- Empty custom nudge remains valid.
- The diagnostic reports effective canonical-fallback behavior without warning/error severity.
- No schema requirement or Pack migration is introduced.
- A focused diagnostic test covers the message.

## Out of scope

Hard validation, generated schema changes, Pack role edits, retry behavior, or another watchdog.

candidates.title: perf(hooks): the per-prompt UserPromptSubmit pair (nudge drain + mail check) rebuilds the city config twice per agent turn, ~1.6 CPU-s after the config-load PRs
candidates.body:
## Summary

Every agent prompt runs two `gc` processes from the projected Claude hooks (`internal/hooks/config/claude.json:35,39`): `gc hook run … -- nudge drain --inject` and `gc hook run … -- mail check --inject`. `gc hook run` re-execs `gc` as a child (`cmd/gc/cmd_hook.go:122`), and each child rebuilds the city config from scratch. After the config-load work already merged (#4565 #4723 #4880 #4682 #4919 #4921 — measured in #6132), the pair still costs **~1.6 CPU-s per agent turn**, and essentially all of it is `loadCityConfig`. That is the term of a host's load that scales with `sessions × turns/min`, and it is paid for two reads whose answer is almost always "nothing".

## Measurements

6-core Intel Mac mini, city with ~57 array tables in `city.toml` and gastown imports, fork of v1.4.0 with the six config-load PRs cherry-picked. `/usr/bin/time -lp`, user+sys including children, medians of 5 interleaved runs:

| verb | CPU-s (with the six PRs) |
|---|---|
| `gc nudge drain --inject` | 1.14 |
| `gc mail check --inject` | 0.46 |
| `bd context --json` (bare, for scale) | 0.16 |

Sampler (`sample`, Go symbols present) on the patched binary: **100 %** of `mail check`'s samples and **~80 %** of `nudge drain`'s are inside `main.loadCityConfig` — recursive `loadPackWithCacheOptions` → `toml.Decode` of pack manifests, `orders.ScanRoots`, `Provenance.captureRevisionSnapshot` (a `git` child per pack), `PackContentHashRecursive`. Page reclaims per process are unchanged by the six PRs (~31k for mail check, ~73k for nudge drain), i.e. what remains is one full config-model rebuild per process, not repeated crossings.

`nudge drain` still shows several store-open instances per run (e.g. from `ackQueuedNudgesWithOutcome`, `cmd/gc/cmd_nudge.go:2264`): the opens now share one code path (`openStoreAtForCityWithAuthority → … → loadCityConfig`) but are not memoised within the process. Each open also runs the preflight: one `bd context --json` child plus one raw Dolt connection for `identity_match`, with no verdict cache on either.

## Why it matters

With N live sessions each averaging T turns/min, the hooks alone burn `N × T × 1.6` CPU-s/min. At 6 sessions and a modest 4 turns/min that is ~0.6 of a core continuously, before any actual work — on a box that also runs the supervisor, the API, and Dolt. Because it is per-turn, it is invisible at idle and appears exactly when the city is busy.

## Proposed direction

In order of leverage:

1. **One process per turn instead of two.** Either a combined verb (`gc hook turn --inject` that runs the drain and the mail check in-process after a single config load), or let `gc hook run` accept both inner argv lists and run them in-process. The hook template then projects one command.
2. **Memoise `loadCityConfig` and the preflight verdict within a process**, so the multiple store opens inside `nudge drain` cost one config build and one `bd context` rather than several.
3. Longer term, #4441's warm controller (bdshim) serving hot verbs is the architectural answer; 1–2 are what can land before that.

I'm raising this as an issue rather than a PR because (1) changes the projected hook contract and I'd rather agree on the shape first.

Related: #6132 (same disease on `gc ready`), #5387, #4924, #4495, #4297.

candidates.title: gc reload prints 'No config changes detected' for an import pin bump that does change effective config
candidates.body:
## Repro

City with a sha-pinned file:// pack import:

```toml
[rigs.imports.support]
source = "file:///path/to/repo//packs/support"
version = "sha:<old>"
```

1. Edit `city.toml` to `version = "sha:<new>"` where `<new>` changes agent pool sizing in the pack.
2. `gc import install` (packs.lock updated, new commit materialized into the cache).
3. `gc reload` → prints **"No config changes detected."**

But the reload demonstrably took effect: `gc agent list --json` immediately reflected the new pool values, `gc status` stopped listing the old pool slots, and open sessions were drift-restarted.

Inconsistently, a *second* pin bump ~30 min later (same procedure) printed the expected `Config reloaded: 15 agents, 1 rigs (rev …)`.

## Why it matters

During a gated config rollout, the operator's confirmation signal is reload output. "No config changes detected" on a change that *did* apply forces out-of-band verification (agent list diffing) and erodes trust in the tool during exactly the operations where confidence matters. Whatever hash/revision comparison gates that message appears not to account for (some path of) import-pin materialization changes.

Observed 2026-07-12 on a fork build based on `faa1d5bd1`; the message and reload path (cmd/gc/city_runtime.go) are present on current upstream `main` (`5774497b0`). Happy to provide trace/timing detail.

candidates.title: Named always session can stay live in reset-pending after config drift
candidates.body:
## Problem

A named `mode=always` session can remain live indefinitely with `reason=reset-pending` after its launch fingerprint changes. The supervisor detects the same config drift on every reconciliation cycle but does not drain or restart the session.

Observed with Gas City 1.4.0 and an OMP Mayor session after `CopyFiles` gained `.gc/scripts`:

- stored fingerprint: `v5:90ef6070f1`
- desired fingerprint: `v5:92ee3a7ee9`
- projected state: `active`, reason `reset-pending`
- repeated supervisor line: `config-drift mayor: stored=v5:90ef6070f1 current=v5:92ee3a7ee9`
- no corresponding Mayor drain, stop, start, panic, or fatal event

An explicit `gc session reset <id>` restores convergence. The session transitions `asleep` -> `creating` -> `active`, receives a new provider session key, clears `continuation_reset_pending`, and stops emitting the drift line.

## Suspected source

`healStatePatchWithRollbackInfo` in `cmd/gc/session_reconcile.go` treats named `mode=always` sessions differently around clearing the provider conversation key, `started_config_hash`, and reset marker. That exception appears to leave a live reset-pending runtime unable to converge after fingerprint drift.

## Expected behavior

For a named `mode=always` session with a live runtime, stale started hash, reset marker, and changed desired hash:

1. The first reconciliation issues exactly one drain.
2. After runtime absence, the next reconciliation clears stale conversation/reset metadata and enqueues one fresh start while preserving bead identity.
3. A successful start stores the new hash and clears reset-pending.
4. Later reconciliation produces no additional drift or drain.

## Separate issue

`gc session logs` can still fail for the reset session when multiple live OMP sessions share the same workdir. Keep that transcript lookup ambiguity separate; unsafe newest-file fallback could return another agent's transcript.

candidates.title: fix(reload): include skill and MCP projections in effective config change detection
candidates.body:
## Summary

City reload reports "No config changes detected." when the only effective change is to FPExtra inputs (skill-file projections and MCP projections), because the reload change-detection compares a config revision that does not cover those inputs. Consumers that refresh on reload revision therefore never see the change.

## Observed evidence

From a live city deployment (Westlands ledger bead `cr-dwveg`):

- Changing only a skill-file projection (an FPExtra input) and triggering a reload produced `No config changes detected.`
- The effective revision stayed equal to the previous one, so no consumer was refreshed even though the effective city configuration had changed.

Suspected comparison site: `cmd/gc/city_runtime.go` — the reload path's no-change branch (the `"No config changes detected."` reply, around line 2040), reached when neither `storeMetadataChanged` nor an order change fired.

## Minimal repro

1. In an isolated city, record the current effective reload revision.
2. Change only a skill-file hash or an MCP projection (no city-config-key or order change).
3. Run reload.
4. Observe: reload reports no changes and the revision is unchanged, so the skill/MCP consumer is not refreshed.

## Expected behavior

The reload effective revision should include every effective input, including skills and MCP projections (FPExtra). A config-noop reload must still report no change, but an FPExtra-only change must produce a new revision and refresh the affected consumer. Add a regression covering config-noop versus FPExtra-only changes.

candidates.title: Support per-rig/per-city CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (account) scoping
candidates.body:
## Summary

No way to scope `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (Claude account/profile) per rig or per city. A single machine-wide supervisor process enforces exactly one `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for every city and rig it manages, and the one mechanism that looks like it should override this per-provider — `providers.<name>.env` in `city.toml` — never actually reaches the spawned session process.

**Goal:** some rigs need a specific Claude account and must never run under a different one by accident. Mixing accounts across rigs is the failure mode to prevent, not just a nice-to-have.

## Root cause

Two compounding issues:

1. **`providers.<name>.env` doesn't propagate.** It resolves correctly in `gc config`/effective-config inspection, but the env vars never reach the actual process spawned for a `tmux`-backed session. Confirmed empirically via an account-email mismatch in a live session's footer — ran under the wrong account despite `providers.<name>.env` being set to override it.
2. **The fallback (editing the supervisor's launchd plist directly) doesn't stick.** `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.gascity.supervisor.plist` is written by `gc register` / `gc supervisor install`, snapshotted from **the invoking shell's own environment** at install time. Any manual edit to the plist is silently overwritten the next time `gc register`/`gc restart` runs from a shell with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

Net effect: no supported way to pin an account per rig/city today.

## Repro

**Propagation gap (1):**
1. Configure a named provider with an `env` block setting `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (or another account-identifying var).
2. `[session] provider = "tmux"` (not `herdr`).
3. Spawn a session bound to that provider.
4. Inspect the session's actual environment / account-identifying output (e.g. footer) — reflects the *default* account, not the configured one.

**Plist-snapshot gap (2):**
1. Register a city while `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set to profile A.
2. Manually edit the installed plist's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to profile B, reload launchd.
3. Run `gc register`/`gc restart` again from a shell still exporting profile A.
4. Plist reverts to profile A — manual edit silently discarded.

## Expected

A rig (or at minimum a city) can declare its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and every session spawned for it reliably uses that value — never silently falls back to the supervisor's default account.

## Feature request — possible shapes

- Honor `providers.<name>.env` for the `claude` provider when spawning the tmux pane (fixes gap 1 directly), and let a rig pin which provider/env it uses.
- Or: let rig config declare `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` explicitly, layered onto the supervisor's env before spawning sessions scoped to that rig.
- Either way: **fail loud** (refuse to spawn) rather than silently falling back to the supervisor's default account on mismatch — silent cross-account mixing is the risk being guarded against, not just an ergonomics gap.

## Environment

- Session backend: `tmux` (not tested against `herdr`)
- Workspace provider: `builtin:claude`
- gc version: 1.4.0

## Notes

Discovered running a bare-engine city (no vendored methodology pack) with a fixed single-session `pm` role, and a separately-managed rig that needed to stay on its own Claude account. Current workaround: manually edit the plist + explicitly export the right `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in the shell before every `gc register`/`gc restart` — fragile, easy to regress.

candidates.title: evals/1d: pricing seam — PricingProvider interface + config overrides
candidates.body:
Sub-issue of #1184. See the umbrella's 1d section for the full design.

## Scope

Establish per-model pricing as a named policy seam — required by 1a's `cost_usd_estimate` and 1b's `agent.invocation.cost_usd`. No pricing infrastructure exists today.

## Design

- **`PricingProvider` optional interface** in `internal/runtime/runtime.go` — separate interface, **not** a method on the 20+ method core `Provider` contract. Follows the established pattern of `IdleWaitProvider`, `DialogProvider`. Providers implement it to expose default rates; absence falls through to user-supplied entries.
- **User overrides via config.** City- and pack-level pricing overrides resolve through the existing layered config machinery. Operators can correct stale defaults without waiting on a release.
- **Schema carries `last_verified` per model.** `gc costs` and the dashboard warn when verification is older than a configurable threshold.
- **Separate rates** for prompt tokens, cache-read tokens, cache-creation tokens. Claude cache-read is ~10× cheaper than prompt; conflating produces badly wrong numbers.
- **`cost_usd_estimate` labeled as an estimate everywhere.** Field name, payload doc, CLI output, dashboard column. Decision-support, not invoice reconciliation.

## Non-goal

A hard-coded Go pricing table.

## Exit criteria

- `PricingProvider` interface defined; Claude provider implements it with current public rates and a `last_verified` date.
- Config layer accepts per-model overrides at city and pack scope.
- 1a's `cost_usd_estimate` and 1b's `agent.invocation.cost_usd` consume the same seam.
- `gc costs` (or equivalent) emits a stale-rates warning when `last_verified` exceeds threshold.

## Open question

Pricing authority for provider defaults — maintainer-curated within each provider package, or community-contributable? Not blocking initial landing; resolve in this sub-issue.

candidates.title: City should survive session logout (keep-alive config)
candidates.body:
## Problem

The city dies when systemd kills user processes overnight. The tmux scope gets cleaned up by logind when no active login session exists.

## Current workaround

`loginctl enable-linger $USER` — prevents systemd from killing user processes after logout.

## Desired behavior

The city config should have a keep-alive option (e.g. `keep_alive = true` or `run_as = "service"`) that:
1. Automatically enables linger on `gc start` if needed
2. Optionally installs a systemd user service for the supervisor
3. Warns on `gc doctor` if the city is running without linger enabled

This ensures the city survives laptop lid-close, display manager session teardown, and SSH disconnects without manual sysadmin steps.

## Context

City died at 00:59:46 on 2026-03-24 when systemd cleaned up the tmux scope (1.2G memory peak). All sessions stopped simultaneously. No OOM, no reboot — just logind killing user processes.

candidates.title: perf(cli): gc ready re-loads the city config and re-spawns bd context once per store it opens
candidates.body:
## Summary

`gc ready` loads the city config at `cmd_ready.go:260` and then opens every store it needs with the
*non-config* helpers, so each open re-loads the whole city config again and rebuilds its own
`bd context --json` preflight reader. The config-taking helpers already exist upstream
(`openStoreAtForCityWithConfig`, `main.go:1555`), the conformance test that polices this rule already
exists, and the ready path is simply the unconverted caller.

## Symptom

`gc ready` cost scales with the number of stores it opens, not with the work it answers. One
federated invocation performs one city-store open plus one open per standalone rig leg, and pays a
fresh `loadCityConfig` (builtin-cache readiness and pack expansion included) and a fresh
`bd context --json` subprocess per open.

On one 16-pool city this is on a controller-cadence path: 16 `scale_check` lines, five of them
`gc ready --include-ephemeral … --json --limit 0` demand probes (`city.toml:966, 977, 1002, 1008,
1196`), across the city store, two rig stores and the class binding. Each `gc` CLI start is measured
there at ~10 dolt connections and ~350 MB RSS (beads#4102, `city.toml:332-336`), and the accumulated
effect at the night seam was recorded as "27 demand-probe shells piled up (oldest 4 min)" — the
operator's mitigation was `probe_concurrency = 3` (`city.toml:259-263`), i.e. a config band-aid for
this code gap.

## Reproduction

Code-level, against `main` = `9d59e5c1041805a78c0f53f8923cc73ff549ba1f`:

```bash
git show origin/main:cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go | sed -n '260,273p'   # cfg loaded, then NOT passed to the opens
git show origin/main:cmd/gc/city_runtime.go | sed -n '3966,3982p'  # cfg in hand, calls openStoreAtForCity
git show origin/main:cmd/gc/main.go | sed -n '1597,1632p'      # cfg==nil -> loadCityConfig; new preflight checker per open
git show origin/main:cmd/gc/beads_preflight_checker.go | sed -n '13,30p'  # BDContext reader spawns bd context, uncached
git show origin/main:cmd/gc/native_dolt_env_cfg_reuse_test.go | rg -n '^func Test'   # 4 guards, none on the ready path
```

Runtime-level (Linux):

```bash
strace -f -e trace=execve gc --city <city> ready --json --limit 0 2>&1 | grep -c 'bd context'
# macOS: sudo fs_usage -f exec | grep 'bd context' during one invocation
```

Result: `expected one config load and one context preflight per invocation` → got: one of each per
store opened (city store + one per standalone rig leg).

## Root cause

`gc ready` already holds the config and does not thread it:

- `cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go:260` `cfg, err := loadCityConfig(cityPath, stderr)`, then
  `cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go:267` `openCityStoreAt(cityPath)` — no `cfg` — and
  `cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go:272` `readyRigLegStores(cfg, cityPath)`.
- `openCityStoreAt` (`cmd/gc/main.go:1471`) → `openCityStoreResultAt` (`:1479`) →
  `openStoreResultAtForCity(cityPath, cityPath)` → nil config → `cmd/gc/main.go:1603`
  `cfg, _ = loadCityConfig(runtimeCityPath, io.Discard)`.
- `readyRigLegStores` (`cmd/gc/ready_federation.go:229`) → `openStandaloneRigStores(cfg, cityPath)`
  (`cmd/gc/city_runtime.go:3966`) → **`cmd/gc/city_runtime.go:3981`
  `openStoreAtForCity(rig.Path, cityPath)`** — that caller has `cfg` as a parameter and still calls
  the loading variant. `openStoreAtForCity` (`cmd/gc/main.go:1546`) forwards
  `openStoreAtForCityWithAuthority(…, false)` → nil cfg → the same `loadCityConfig` at `:1603`.
- The same open path rebuilds the preflight reader every time: `cmd/gc/main.go:1630`
  `PreflightChecker: newBeadsPreflightChecker(runtimeCityPath, provider)` →
  `cmd/gc/beads_preflight_checker.go:17` `BDContext: preflightBDContextReader(cityPath)` →
  `:23` runs `bd context --json` through `bdCommandRunnerForCity(cityPath)`. There is no cache:
  `cachedPreflightBDContextReader` appears in 0 files. Note the reader is already
  scope-parameterised (`func(scope string) …`), so per-scope isolation of a shared cached reader is
  part of the same atom, not an extra.
- The rule is this repo's own: `cmd/gc/native_dolt_env_cfg_reuse_test.go` exists precisely to
  enforce "reuse the config you were given" and carries exactly four guards (`:18`, `:107`, `:166`,
  `:215` — `TestOpenNativeStoreReusesTheLoadedCityConfig`, `TestBdBeadExistsProbeReusesTheLoadedCityConfig`,
  `TestWorkRecordCloseGateReusesTheLoadedCityConfig`, `TestBdCloseGateReusesTheWriteGuardsStoreRead`).
  **None covers the ready path.** The precedent is #4723 (merged 2026-07-29), which converted
  `cmd_bd.go` / `work_record_gate.go` / `store_target_exec.go` and added that test file; the ready
  path was not in that pass.
- The parallel half is also unfurnished: `cmd/gc/ready_federation.go` has zero `sync.` / `go func` /
  `errgroup` hits at `main`, so the leg fan-out is a serial per-leg loop.

## Fix candidates

**A. Thread the loaded config and one cached context preflight through the ready path** — open the
city store and every rig leg via the existing `openStoreAtForCityWithConfig` (`cmd/gc/main.go:1555`)
/ `openStoreResultAtForCityWithConfig` (`:1597`), build one cached BD-context reader per invocation
and pass it down (the BD-context-taking variant does **not** exist yet — 0 hits for
`WithConfigAndBDContext` — so that part is additive), and add the two ready-path guards to the
existing conformance file (e.g. `TestReadyRigStoreOpenReusesTheLoadedCityConfig`,
`TestCmdReadySharesOneBDContextPreflightAcrossCityAndRigOpens`).
- Scope: `cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go`, `cmd/gc/main.go`, `cmd/gc/ready_federation.go`,
  `cmd/gc/beads_preflight_checker.go`, +2 tests.
- Trade-off: the store-open helpers gain a parameter, so every caller must pass it — which is the
  point of the guard: the unconverted call site becomes a compile-time or test-time failure instead
  of a silent per-store reload.

**B. Memoize at the lowest layer** — cache the loaded city config and the `bd context` read
process-wide keyed by city path, leaving call sites unchanged.
- Scope: ~1 file.
- Trade-off: no signature churn, but a process-wide cache is exactly what the existing
  "reuse the config you were given" rule avoids, and it hides the unconverted call site instead of
  converting it.

**Recommendation: A**, because it is the same change #4723 already made for the other CLI paths and
the config-taking helper is sitting there unused by this caller — that is what makes it cheap to
accept. Maintainer's call.

## Adjacent / out of scope

- **#6013** (open PR, `perf(cli): stop eagerly reloading city config on every control-ready tick`)
  is the same defect shape at a different door: `dispatch_control_ready.go` only. Coordinate, do not
  merge the two issues.
- **#5540** (open PR) pins the native-Dolt pool ceiling to 1 conn for one-shot store opens — that is
  the *connection* half of the symptom and does not touch the redundant config loads or the repeated
  `bd context` spawn.
- **#5903** (open PR) touches `cmd/gc/cmd_ready.go`, `cmd_ready_test.go` and
  `schemas/ready/result.schema.json`; a ready-path change should rebase on that file's final shape
  rather than hand-merge.
- **#5539** (connection churn from one-shot CLI opens), **#5533** (serial `bd` discovery in the hook
  budget), **#5712** (per-identity duplicate scans in the generated work query) and **#5519** (`git
  status` per pack source on every command) are neighbours in the per-invocation-floor family, each a
  different call site. This issue names only the ready path's config load and context preflight.
- `cmd/gc/ready_federation.go`'s serial leg loop is named above as still-true, but the fix proposed
  here is the reuse conversion; parallelism is a separate call.

candidates.title: feat(config): wire cloudflare provider into city.toml
candidates.body:
## Summary

`provider = "cloudflare"` currently requires setting `GC_CLOUDFLARE_RUNTIME_URL` and `GC_CLOUDFLARE_RUNTIME_TOKEN` as environment variables. Every other provider (acp, k8s) reads from city.toml. This issue tracks making Cloudflare first-class in the config.

## Proposed config shape

```toml
[session]
provider = "cloudflare"

[session.cloudflare]
url   = "https://my-worker.workers.dev"
token = "secret"   # optional; prefer env for the secret (see below)
```

## Work required

- Add `CloudflareConfig { URL, Token string }` to `internal/config.SessionConfig` alongside the existing `ACP` field.
- Map TOML `url` → `CloudflareConfig.URL` → `cloudflare.Config.Endpoint` (the provider field is `Endpoint`, not `URL` — the wiring must translate explicitly).
- Pass through `newSessionProviderByName` → `NewProviderWithConfig`.
- Precedence follows Gas City convention: city.toml is the base; `GC_CLOUDFLARE_RUNTIME_URL` / `GC_CLOUDFLARE_RUNTIME_TOKEN` override when set (consistent with K8s, beads, session selector).
- Enforce `https://` only when a token is present (compatible with existing `http://` test servers that pass no token).
- Regenerate JSON schema via `cmd/genschema` after adding `CloudflareConfig` to `SessionConfig`.
- Check `internal/config/undecoded.go` allowlist for the new `[session.cloudflare]` table.
- Update `newSessionProviderByName` godoc to list `"cloudflare"`.

## Secrets note

`token` in TOML is plaintext on disk. Recommend keeping the secret in `GC_CLOUDFLARE_RUNTIME_TOKEN` via env and using TOML only for `url`.

## Depends on

#2543

candidates.title: feat: config: implicit provider agents get no default lifecycle/max_active_sessions, forcing per-rig patches.agent boilerplate
candidates.body:
## Summary

`InjectImplicitAgents` creates rig-scoped implicit provider agents with no `Lifecycle` and no `MaxActiveSessions`, and `ApplyAgentDefaults`/`[agent_defaults]` has no way to supply either. Operators who want a one-shot lifecycle and a session cap on a provider that is imported into several rigs must write one near-identical `[[patches.agent]]` block per rig, purely to repeat the same two values.

## Symptom

In a multi-rig city that imports the same one-shot provider (e.g. `claude-sonnet-one-shot`) into several rigs, each rig needs its own explicit patch just to set `lifecycle = "one_shot"` and `max_active_sessions = N`:

```toml
[[patches.agent]]
name = "claude-sonnet-one-shot"
rig = "fable-nomad"
provider = "claude-sonnet-one-shot"
lifecycle = "one_shot"
max_active_sessions = 8

[[patches.agent]]
name = "claude-sonnet-one-shot"
rig = "fable-nomad-research"
provider = "claude-sonnet-one-shot"
lifecycle = "one_shot"
max_active_sessions = 3
```

Without the patch, the rig-scoped implicit agent gets `Lifecycle == ""` (long-lived session semantics) and `MaxActiveSessions == nil` (uncapped), which is usually wrong for a provider meant to run bounded one-shot work — so the boilerplate is not optional, it's a workaround for a missing default.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a provider under `[providers.<name>]`.
2. Import it into two or more rigs (no explicit `[[agents]]` block for it in any rig).
3. Run config composition (`InjectImplicitAgents` then `ApplyAgentDefaults`).
4. Inspect the resulting rig-scoped `Agent` for that provider in each rig.

Expected: a way to declare "this provider is one-shot with cap N" once, and have every rig-scoped implicit agent for that provider inherit it.
Got: `Lifecycle` is always `""` and `MaxActiveSessions` is always `nil` on implicit agents; the only way to set them is a full `[[patches.agent]]` block per `(name, rig)` pair.

## Root cause

`InjectImplicitAgents` (`internal/config/config.go:3695`) constructs both city-scoped and rig-scoped implicit `Agent` values without ever setting `Lifecycle` or `MaxActiveSessions`:

```go
cfg.Agents = append(cfg.Agents, Agent{
    Name:                name,
    Dir:                 rig.Name,
    Provider:            name,
    PromptTemplate:      promptTemplate,
    DefaultSlingFormula: &slingFormula,
    Implicit:            true,
})
```
(`internal/config/config.go:3742-3749`, rig-scoped loop; the city-scoped loop at `internal/config/config.go:3727-3734` has the same gap.)

`ApplyAgentDefaults` (`internal/config/config.go:3796`) runs after injection and back-fills `Provider`, `DefaultSlingFormula`, and `Upstream` from `[agent_defaults]` for any agent that didn't set its own value — but `AgentDefaults` (`internal/config/config.go:3059`) has no `Lifecycle` or `MaxActiveSessions` field, so there is nothing for it to back-fill from even if the injected agent left them zero-valued.

`Agent.Lifecycle` (`internal/config/config.go:3238-3241`) and `Agent.MaxActiveSessions` (`internal/config/config.go:3263-3266`) are ordinary per-agent fields with no config-level default path — every other injected-agent knob (`DefaultSlingFormula`, `Provider`, `Upstream`) has one via `[agent_defaults]`, these two don't.

## Fix candidates

**A. Add `Lifecycle` and `MaxActiveSessions` to `AgentDefaults`, apply in `ApplyAgentDefaults`** — mirror the existing `DefaultSlingFormula` pattern: add `Lifecycle string` and `MaxActiveSessions *int` to `AgentDefaults` (`internal/config/config.go:3059`), and in `ApplyAgentDefaults` set them on any agent whose own field is still the zero value, skipping `ControlDispatcherAgentName` as the other loops already do.
- Scope: ~20-30 LOC in `internal/config/config.go`, plus a schema/doc update for `[agent_defaults]` and a composition test.
- Trade-off: consistent with the existing `DefaultSlingFormula`/`Upstream`/`Provider` precedent (explicit agent value always wins); city-wide only, so a city that legitimately wants different caps per rig for the *same* provider still needs per-rig patches — but the common case (one lifecycle/cap per provider) collapses to one line.

**B. Add a provider-level default: `[providers.<name>].lifecycle` / `.max_active_sessions`, applied by `InjectImplicitAgents` at agent-creation time** — since the boilerplate is keyed by provider, not by rig, let the provider declaration itself carry the default lifecycle/cap, and have `InjectImplicitAgents` (`internal/config/config.go:3695`) set `Lifecycle`/`MaxActiveSessions` on each created `Agent` directly from the provider it derives from.
- Scope: ~15-25 LOC in `internal/config/config.go` plus the provider struct/schema, similar size to A.
- Trade-off: matches the mental model "this provider is inherently one-shot" more closely than a city-wide `agent_defaults` value, and doesn't require touching `ApplyAgentDefaults`; but it's a new provider-level knob (larger schema surface) versus reusing the existing `agent_defaults` extension point.

**Recommendation:** A, because it reuses the `[agent_defaults]` precedent already established for `DefaultSlingFormula`/`Upstream`/`Provider` instead of adding a new config surface, and is a smaller diff. Maintainer's call.

## Adjacent / out of scope

- `[[patches.agent]]` already supports deferred patching onto implicit agents (#2203 / PR #3587) — this issue is about removing the need for the patch in the common single-value-per-provider case, not about patch mechanics.
- The rig-copy `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` dedupe mentioned in our internal tracking is a separate concern (no supported per-rig override mechanism exists yet) and is not part of this issue.

candidates.title: feat(runtime): gc should derive codex provider config and provision a writable provider home
candidates.body:
### Problem to solve

Gas City wires provider **env** for an agent, but not provider **config files**
or a writable provider home. Running codex on Kubernetes we had to hand-seed both
from a shell `pre_start`:

- `~/.codex/config.toml`, defining a custom model provider pointed at our
  OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible proxy (`requires_openai_auth = false`,
  `wire_api = "responses"`), so codex uses API-key auth and skips ChatGPT
  onboarding.
- `CODEX_HOME` plus `XDG_{CACHE,DATA,STATE,RUNTIME}` pinned to paths writable by
  the pod's non-root user, with a `chown` in `pre_start`. Without this, codex
  could not write its runtime state and failed to start its app-server at all.

Defining a custom model provider is legitimate configuration. Having to express
it as a shell heredoc, and having to discover that the container's default
provider home is not writable by the agent user, is not.

### Proposed change

- **Derive codex provider config from `[providers.codex]`** the way gc already
  derives env. If gc knows the base URL and auth mode, it can materialize the
  provider's config file rather than making each operator write one.
- **Provision a writable provider home for the pod user** in the k8s runtime, so
  `CODEX_HOME`/XDG pinning is not an operator responsibility.

### Alternatives considered

- **Document the `pre_start` recipe.** Better than nothing, but it makes every
  operator responsible for a file format owned by the CLI vendor, and it breaks
  when that format changes.
- **Bake it into the agent image.** Pushes deployment-specific endpoints into an
  image and defeats per-city configuration.

### Scope and impact

- Affects provider resolution and the k8s runtime's pod setup.
- Directly reduces the size of the `pre_start` blob an operator must copy.
- The writable-home half is arguably a plain bug in the k8s runtime.

Found running the Kubernetes provider end-to-end (see the umbrella issue).

candidates.title: bug: config watcher registers a pack root's whole .git subtree, so every git write pokes a no-op reload
candidates.body:
### Before you continue

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I read the relevant docs and contributor guidance.

### Gas City version

`main@58a571faa` (verified against current `main`, not a local branch)

### Environment

Reproduced on Linux (Debian trixie, amd64, inotify backend) with `go test ./cmd/gc/`; the mechanism is backend-independent and the descriptor cost it feeds is macOS/kqueue-specific.

### Summary

`configWatchRegistrar`'s recursive walk prunes with `shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent`, which excludes `.gc` and `.beads` but **not** `.git`. Any recursive watch target that is a git worktree — the shape `gc import add` writes for a local repo path (`canonicalizeLocalGitImportSource`, `internal/importsvc/source.go`), and any pack dir that happens to live inside one — gets its whole `.git` subtree registered as watches: `objects/**`, `refs/**`, `logs/**`.

Nothing under `.git` can change a pack's content hash. The content side already skips it: `isIgnoredPackRuntimePath` (`internal/config/pack.go:3019`) excludes `.beads`, `.cache`, `.gc`, `.git`, `state`, `tmp`, and gates `collectFiles`, which feeds `packContentHashRecursive` (`internal/config/pack.go:2931`). So the watch set is a strict superset of the set that can actually produce a config change.

Because the same predicate also gates event *delivery* (`cmd/gc/controller.go:846`), this is not only wasted watch registrations: every git object, ref, and reflog write enqueues a config reload that is guaranteed to be a no-op, and each reload rebuilds the watcher over the whole tree again (`restartConfigWatcher` → `watchConfigTargets`).

### Reproduction

Add to `cmd/gc/controller_test.go` and run `go test -run RedProof ./cmd/gc/`:

```go
dir := t.TempDir()
os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "pack.toml"), []byte("name = \"sample\"\n"), 0o644)
objectDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "objects", "ab")
os.MkdirAll(objectDir, 0o755)
objectFile := filepath.Join(objectDir, "cdef0123456789")
os.WriteFile(objectFile, []byte("original\n"), 0o644)

var dirty atomic.Bool
pokeCh := make(chan struct{}, 1)
var stderr bytes.Buffer
cleanup := watchConfigTargets([]config.WatchTarget{{Path: dir, Recursive: true}}, &dirty, pokeCh, &stderr)
defer cleanup()
// drain, dirty.Store(false), then:
os.WriteFile(objectFile, []byte("rewritten\n"), 0o644)
select {
case <-pokeCh:
        t.Fatalf("watcher poke fired for a write under .git (dirty=%v)", dirty.Load())
case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
}
```

Observed on `main@58a571faa`:

```
--- FAIL: TestRedProof_GitWriteWakesConfigWatcher
    RED CONFIRMED: watcher poke fired for a write under .git (dirty=true)
```

### Expected behavior

A write under a watched pack root's `.git` directory registers no watch and delivers no config event, because it cannot change the config revision.

### Actual behavior

The whole `.git` subtree is walked and watched, and any write inside it sets the dirty flag and pokes a reload.

### Blast radius

`shouldIgnoreConfigWatchEvent` has exactly two callers, both in `cmd/gc/controller.go`: the recursive walk's `SkipDir` at `:687` and the event-loop filter at `:846`. Nothing else in the tree depends on the config watcher seeing `.git`. Git-backed import freshness is pull-side, not watcher-driven: `remoteCacheFingerprint` (`internal/config/pack_include.go:389`) stats `.git/index` itself on each config load, and deliberately excludes the `.git` *directory* for its own reasons. Working-tree changes from a checkout or pull still fire events, since those files sit outside `.git`.

### Relationship to existing issues

- **#4504** (open, macOS supervisor reload leaks thousands of FDs) — different root cause (pinned `fsnotify v1.9.0`'s kqueue `Close()`, fixed upstream in fsnotify v1.10.0 / fsnotify#740), but this defect is a large multiplier on it: `.git/objects` is usually the biggest directory count under a watched repo root, and it is re-registered on every rebuild. In one local measurement of a 21-directory repo tree, the `.git` subtree accounted for most of the ~54 descriptors leaked per restart cycle.
- **#2954** (closed, FD leak — 51k open handles to rig `node_modules`) — its own diagnostics list `1000 /Users/matt/dev/gascity-pack/.git/objects` as the third-largest FD holder. That issue was fixed on the content-hash side by adding `node_modules` to `isIgnoredPackRuntimePath`; the watch side was never aligned, so both `.git` and `node_modules` are still watched.

### Fix candidates

1. **Add `.git` to the watch exclusion** (what the attached PR does). Keeps the existing any-depth matching that `.gc` and `.beads` already use, and lifts the names into a slice. Smallest change, zero design questions: no config content lives under `.git` at any depth.
2. **Align the watch predicate with `isIgnoredPackRuntimePath` in full**, so the watch set is a subset of the hashed set — this would additionally stop watching `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.cache`, `state`, and `tmp`, closing the other half of #2954. It needs a maintainer's call on semantics: the pack-side list matches `.cache`/`state`/`tmp` only as the first path segment relative to the pack root, while the watch predicate is depth-agnostic and gets absolute paths, so a faithful alignment means passing the pack root through to the predicate rather than reusing it as-is.

I went with (1) because it is the exact shape already established for `.gc` and `.beads` and carries no semantic change; (2) is the larger win and I am happy to follow up on it if you want it.

candidates.title: providers API reports profile-gated model/effort defaults the launcher no longer uses
candidates.body:
Follow-up to #5446 (fixes #5441). Not a regression from that PR — a pre-existing divergence it makes observable.

## Background

#5446 added a profile-aware gate, `suppressPresetModelEffortForProfile` (`internal/config/resolve.go`), applied at both provider-resolution paths: the chain walk's leaf merge (`internal/config/chain.go`) and the two Phase A legacy merges in `lookupProvider` (`internal/config/resolve.go`). When a provider's merged effective args route through a codex `--profile`, the preset-inherited `model` and `effort` OptionDefaults are dropped, because CLI flags outrank the profile's own config and would silently clobber the operator's pins.

Three call sites merge providers **without** that gate.

## Sites

1. **`internal/api/huma_handlers_providers.go:45,47`** — `resolveAllProviders` calls `config.MergeProviderOverBuiltin` for both the name-match and command-match cases, mirroring the two now-gated sites in `lookupProvider`, but ungated.

2. **`internal/api/handler_providers.go:92`** — `toProviderPublicResponse` recomputes `resp.EffectiveDefaults = config.ComputeEffectiveDefaults(spec.OptionsSchema, spec.OptionDefaults, nil)` from that ungated merged spec.

   Net effect: `GET /v0/city/{cityName}/providers/public` advertises `model=gpt-5.5` / `effort=xhigh` for exactly the providers where the launcher now drops them.

3. **`internal/config/resolved_cache.go:101,105`** — the same ungated merge. Harmless today: the suppression only ever removes keys, so validation sees a superset of valid values and cannot fail falsely. Worth folding in for consistency rather than leaving a second copy of the merge that disagrees with `lookupProvider`.

## Impact

Display-only. The launcher path (`BuildProviderLaunchCommand` and resume-command completion) is gated and correct; the API reports defaults that differ from what is actually launched, so the dashboard shows a model/effort the session will not use.

## Fix shape

- Export a narrowly scoped resolution helper from `internal/config` so `internal/api` applies the same gate instead of re-deriving the merge itself. `resolved_cache.go` is in package `config` and can call the unexported `suppressPresetModelEffortForProfile` directly.
- Add an API test with a city provider whose `args_append = ["exec", "--profile", "pin-model"]`, asserting the public effective defaults omit `model` and `effort` while retaining `permission_mode`.

Deliberately kept out of #5446: the API change needs a new exported helper plus a test in a different package, which is scope growth on a tight config-layer bugfix.
